title: Strict mode
subtitle: strict bundle, null checks, implicit any, class init

cards.front: Is strict: true one compiler check?
cards.meaning: No. It is a shortcut that turns on a bundle: strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, strictPropertyInitialization, useUnknownInCatchVariables, alwaysStrict, noImplicitThis, and strictBindCallApply. Interviews want the bundle named, then the important ones unpacked.

cards.front: Can you turn one flag off under strict: true?
cards.meaning: Yes — enable strict and set an individual flag false while migrating (e.g. "strictNullChecks": false under "strict": true). Possible, but discouraged long-term.

cards.front: Which strict flag matters most, and what is second?
cards.meaning: strictNullChecks has the biggest real-world impact — without it null/undefined are silently assignable everywhere. noImplicitAny is a close second — it stops untyped parameters from becoming implicit any.

null and undefined are only assignable where the type allows them. Without it, string secretly means string | null | undefined in practice, so the type system stops protecting you from reading a property of null/undefined.

cards.front: getLength(null) without strictNullChecks — compile or crash?
cards.meaning: It compiles and crashes at runtime. With strictNullChecks, null is not assignable to string.
cards.example: function getLength(s: string) { return s.length; } getLength(null); // compiles without the flag, errors with it

cards.front: How do you accept null under strictNullChecks?
cards.meaning: Type the parameter as string | null and narrow before use. After if (s === null) return 0, s.length is string.
cards.example: function getLengthSafe(s: string | null) { if (s === null) return 0; return s.length; }

cards.front: What must APIs do once strictNullChecks is on?
cards.meaning: Say string | null when null is possible, then narrow (if, ??, optional chaining). Optional chaining does not replace modeling | null. prop?: T already involves undefined under the flag.

cards.front: What happens to function log(x) under noImplicitAny?
cards.meaning: Error: parameter 'x' implicitly has an 'any' type. With the flag off, x is implicitly any and checking is largely off for x. With it on, you annotate (or rely on context typing) so any is an explicit choice.
cards.example: function log(x) {} // error with noImplicitAny; function log(x: string) {} // ok

cards.front: Why does noImplicitAny matter beyond one parameter?
cards.meaning: any infects call sites. One untyped callback parameter can disable checking through a whole chain. The flag forces annotations or inference from context so any is not a silent default.
No. Context typing still works: .map((n) => n + 1) on number[] infers n without an annotation.

cards.front: Does strict or noImplicitAny ban all any?
cards.meaning: No. Explicit any is still allowed. noImplicitAny blocks inferred any on untyped parameters and similar holes, not every intentional any annotation — use those sparingly.

cards.front: What else is in the strict bundle besides null checks and noImplicitAny?
cards.meaning: strictFunctionTypes: callback params checked more strictly (a string-only handler is not assignable to string | number). strictPropertyInitialization: class fields must be initialized in the declaration or constructor. useUnknownInCatchVariables (in the bundle since TS 4.4): catch (e) is unknown. alwaysStrict: emit/parse JS "use strict". noImplicitThis: untyped this is an error, not any. strictBindCallApply: bind/call/apply args must match the function.

cards.front: How do you fix uninitialized Nest class fields under strictPropertyInitialization?
cards.meaning: Give a default (private users: User[] = []), use definite assignment sparingly (private users!: User[]), or initialize via a constructor parameter property for DI. Parameter properties already count as initialized.
cards.example: private users: User[] = [];  // or users!;  // or constructor(private readonly repo: UserRepository) {}

cards.front: When is private users!: User[] acceptable?
cards.meaning: Only when something else definitely assigns before read (framework DI, a lifecycle you control). Abuse of ! reintroduces null crashes under a lie to the compiler. Do not spam ! on every Nest property.

cards.front: Is TypeScript strict the same as JS "use strict"?
cards.meaning: No. TypeScript strict is the type-check bundle. JS "use strict" is runtime language mode. They meet via alwaysStrict in the bundle — do not treat strictNullChecks as "use strict".

cards.front: Migrating a non-strict app — fix which flags first?
cards.meaning: Turn on strict, then fix strictNullChecks and noImplicitAny first — largest bug surface. Turning off strictNullChecks “to ship faster” gives null/undefined silent assignability again.
